text:
maya: Quick check — Savant8B int8 smoke results are in. ~18% token cost savings vs fp16 but we're seeing a recall hit on long-context (>1024) multi-turns. shared eval gist: https://short.link/savant8b-eval :thinking_face:

sam: Can you paste the slice numbers? which metrics moved?

maya: Sure — short summary (slice, metric, fp16 -> int8):
```
long_form_qa, mrr, 0.912 -> 0.856
summarization_long, rougeL, 0.435 -> 0.402
short_chat, mrr, 0.881 -> 0.878
```
More detail in the gist.

eval-bot: Automated report: BER +3.2, MRR overall -4.9%, long-context MRR -6.1%, median latency +0.8ms, p90 latency unchanged. CI (95%) on slices attached.

priya: Does this look like a priming / positional embedding quant sensitivity? KV-cache hops?

maya: Likely. We ran static quant with per-channel symmetric; saw heavier degradation when priming length > 800 tokens. I re-ran with eval prompt truncation and recall improves ~2 pts but loses user-visible context.

sam: Two actionable paths: 1) ops-level routing: keep int8 for short sessions, fallback to fp16/dedicated for long sessions; 2) try quant config tweaks (dynamic range, group size=64). Which is faster to ship?

maya: Routing is faster. Quant retune needs more bench time. My perf numbers: int8 cost per 1M tokens = $22, fp16 = $27 (hosted unit econ).

jack: From product: what's the GTN recommendation? If we save ~$5/1M tokens but lose ~6% MRR on long flows, that's risky for high-value customers. Can we A/B canary?

priya: Yes — canary plan: 5% traffic int8 with traffic split by session length flag. Monitor KL divergence on top-k and MRR on our primary slices. If delta(MRR) <= 2% within 48h, expand to 25%.

maya: Proposed immediate rollout:
- Canary: 5% traffic, only sessions <=1024 tokens go to int8.
- Fallback: if long_context flag true OR eval-bot drift alarm fires, route to fp16.
- Ops: enable prefix caching to reduce long-session tokens where possible.

sam: Also try a small quant retune with group size 64 + outlier clamp — run on 10k sample pool, low effort (2-3 hours). If it recovers >3% on long_form_qa, we can widen int8 to 20% for short+medium.

jack: Sounds good. Product OK with canary if monitoring dashboards are live and alert thresholds set.

priya: I'll wire the alert: MRR_long > -3% threshold, KL_topk > 0.08. Will post runbook.

maya: I'll kick off canary and the quick retune. Sharing the canary config here:```json
{ "route": "int8", "max_session_tokens": 1024, "traffic_pct": 5 }
```

sam: Small note — update batching policy for int8 path to batch_size=8 to keep latency sweet spot.

jack: Approve. Go for canary. Keep product looped if we hit user-visible regressions. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — will update with first 24h snapshot.
